inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio (links AVFAudio), VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For the aquarium (checked 2026-11-14): VisualCoreSimulation has SeededRandom, FixedStepClock, FixedStepRunner (FixedStepSimulation), ParticleSystem with Emitter, EmitterShape (point, line, ring), EmitterBurst and ParticleForce (gravity, drag, attractor, repulsor, gravityWell, wind, vortex); VisualCoreScenes has the 2D SceneNode tree with Primitive rect, circle, line, polygon (<= 256 points) and polyline (<= 8,192 points), hit testing, PointerTracker, the tap, double-tap, long-press, drag, pinch and rotate recognizers and GestureArbiter; VisualCoreMath has Camera2D, PlaneViewport and EasingCurve; VisualCoreRendering has PrimitiveRenderer (one batched triangle list per tree), ParticleRenderer with ParticleBlend (normal, additive), ParticleLayerScene and TrailLayer. No neighbour search (spatial hash or grid) and no steering or flocking exists in any product (grep 2026-11-14).

RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler and context generations; pause/resume, replaceScene, recreateContext, renderOffscreen and destroy; scenes implement RenderScene setup/resize/render/teardown. All EGL and GL work runs on the main thread. The aquarium's fixed-step simulation (school movement, food, bubbles) is CPU work stepped on the main thread at the frame boundary; only finished instance and vertex data is uploaded. Digital Aquarium adds no EGL or GL context of its own.

ResourceRegistry creates buffers, textures, programs and render targets under a ResourceBudget and rejects stale handles after a generation change. ShaderProgram, ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary (#include expansion with line maps) compile bundled GLSL; the vc/ library holds color, field, hash, noise, palette and sdf helpers. PrimitiveRenderer draws a 2D SceneNode tree as one batched triangle list through Camera2D; ParticleRenderer draws particle instances in one batch; TrailLayer keeps a fading image; FullScreenShaderScene and the effects graph (copy, colorMatrix, blur, bloom, distort, composite, feedback, flashLimit; EffectScene, EffectRenderer) complete the 2D drawing set.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies the quality level (QualityGovernor over the experience's QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions thermal state and Low Power Mode) and memory/scene-phase events; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls) to Experience; ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state; ExperienceStorage is the per-experience sandbox; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (Digital Aquarium joins in A09-P01; it stays unregistered and unavailable in A09-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets). Digital Aquarium needs no microphone, camera, photos or location, so no usage description or privacy answer changes.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 98 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-14 (shared checks, package and app builds/tests, per-experience release, copy-claims and verify steps of A01-A08 on iOS 27 and 26, release audits of the one app, the seven reference regression steps).

Digital Aquarium owns its domain (habitat document, species catalog with two procedural species, plants and decor, fish shapes and swim animation, feeding, decoration placement, depth layers, bubbles and caustics composition, the ambient low-motion mode with dimming and the spoken habitat description) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/DigitalAquarium/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders; created in A09-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: the seeded fixed-step clock, particles, forces and the bounded steering with a neighbour search to come (VisualCoreSimulation), 2D shapes and gestures (VisualCoreScenes, drawn by VisualCoreRendering), effect passes (VisualCoreEffects; a caustics pattern moves there only if it proves reusable), quality, persistence and storage (constitution Principle II, A09 section). ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in docs/apps/digital-aquarium/regression-baseline.md.

FixedStepClock (default 1/120 s, at most 8 steps per frame, interpolation alpha) and FixedStepRunner over a FixedStepSimulation with a ControlStream of commands give deterministic, frame-rate-independent stepping; SeededRandom (SplitMix64) and SeedDerivation give reproducible per-entity streams; ParticleSystem steps seeded emitters and forces with a bounded capacity (default 10,000, max 100,000). Particle Universe (A04) runs its SceneSimulation this way; Digital Aquarium's school, food and bubble state will step the same way, so a habitat replays identically from its seed.

matrix.capability: Sprite and object systems: many independent 2D objects (fish bodies, fins, plants, rocks, decor) as SceneNode shapes with transform, z order, visibility, colour and hit testing, batched into one premultiplied triangle list per tree on the main thread
matrix.source: brainstorm: sprite and object systems; v0.1 feature 01; manual risk draw overhead
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests/SceneGraphTests and VisualCoreRenderingTests/PrimitiveRendererTests. Draw overhead: every node of a tree lands in one batch (one draw), polygons are capped at 256 points and polylines at 8,192; the audit does not measure performance (spec edge case). Sprites are procedural shapes, never bitmap art.

matrix.capability: Animation: deterministic seeded fixed-step clock and runner with interpolation alpha, easing curves and per-entity seeded streams
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests (FixedStepClock, FixedStepRunner, SeededRandom) and VisualCoreMathTests (easing).

matrix.capability: Procedural fish shapes and swim animation: per-species outline built from parameters (body length, depth, tail, fins, palette), a travelling body wave and tail beat tied to speed, smooth turning, drawn as polygons per frame
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 02; brainstorm: animation, sprite and object systems; manual P02 fish movement and visual prototype
matrix.notes: The polygon primitive, transforms and the fixed-step clock exist and are tested; no outline generator or body-wave deformation exists, and both are species-specific. G-FISHSWIM (app-local), A09-P02. Built in A09-P02 (app-local): AquariumPresenter draws each fish from its species outline with a body wave of 0.06 body lengths, a tail sweep of 0.15 body lengths driven by the speed-scaled animation phase, and a bend toward the smoothed turn capped at ±0.35 rad; Reduce Motion halves all three in drawing only (AquariumRenderTests).

matrix.capability: Bounded school behaviours: steering forces (separation, alignment, cohesion, wander, boundary avoidance) with speed and turn-rate limits over a bounded neighbour search (uniform grid or spatial hash with a per-agent neighbour cap)
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 02; manual risk erratic motion; spec FR-A09-003
matrix.notes: ParticleForce has only point and field forces (gravity, drag, attractor, repulsor, gravityWell, wind, vortex) applied to particles independently; no agent-to-agent force, neighbour query, spatial hash or grid, or steering/flocking exists in any framework product (grep 2026-11-14). Steering with a bounded neighbour search is generic (schools, swarms, crowds), so it belongs to VisualCoreSimulation. G-STEERING, A09-P02. Built in A09-P02 (upstream, VisualCoreSimulation): NeighbourSearch (linear scan, at most limit neighbours within a radius, nearest first, ties by index) and Steering (separation over all neighbours, alignment and cohesion within a group, inward boundary push, each term and the sum capped); AquariumSimulation schools the fish with species tuning, a reduced seeded wander and the Phase 01 bounds and speed limits (SteeringForceTests, NeighbourSearchTests, SchoolingTests). A grid was not needed for 24 fish.

matrix.capability: Procedural environments: water gradient background, sand, rocks and plants drawn in code from noise, SDF and palette helpers, full-screen shader scenes and polygons
matrix.notes: FullScreenShaderScene, ShaderLibrary (vc/noise, vc/sdf, vc/palette) and Palette are tested in their own test targets; the habitat's layout and plant sway are experience domain (G-HABITAT for the document, G-FISHSWIM for motion).

matrix.capability: Particles: seeded emitters (point, line, ring, bursts) with forces and a capacity bound, drawn in one batch with normal or additive blending
matrix.notes: Built for A04; tested in VisualCoreSimulationTests/ParticleSystemTests and VisualCoreRenderingTests (ParticleRendererTests, ParticleLayerSceneTests).

matrix.capability: Scene management: one render host, RenderScene lifecycle, scene replacement without a second context, presenter adapter and a fitted 2D camera for the tank
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRenderingTests, VisualCoreExperienceHostTests and VisualCoreMathTests.

matrix.capability: Touch interaction: tap, double-tap, long-press, drag and pinch recognizers with arbitration, multi-pointer tracking and hit testing of scene nodes
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests (GestureTests, PointerTrackerTests, SceneGraphTests hitTestFindsTopmostVisibleShape); RenderView+Touches feeds pointer events.

matrix.capability: One complete aquarium with two fish species and plants: a habitat document (tank bounds, seed, species catalog of two procedural species with counts, plant and decor placements, lighting) built deterministically from its seed
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 01; manual P01 habitat model
matrix.notes: Shapes, seeds and palettes exist; the habitat schema, the two species and their limits are Digital Aquarium's domain, as Particle Universe's SceneDocument is A04's. G-HABITAT (app-local), A09-P01. Built in A09-P01 (app-local): HabitatDocument schema 1 (tank 16 × 9, swim bounds, fish, plants, decor, lighting) built by HabitatDocument.starter from SpeciesCatalog.bundled (four species, four plant kinds, two starter habitats Reef and Kelp with two species each) and a SeededRandom; AquariumSimulation keeps every fish inside the bounds (HabitatDocumentTests, SpeciesCatalogTests, AquariumSimulationTests: 10,000 steps × 20 seeds).

matrix.capability: Tap-to-feed and decoration placement: a tap drops food that sinks and is eaten (fish seek the nearest pellet), decor is placed, moved and removed within tank bounds by long-press and drag with hit testing and a bounded count
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 03; manual P03 editing, feeding and save system
matrix.notes: Gestures, hit testing and view-to-world conversion exist and are tested; food pellets, seeking and the placement rules are experience domain over the shared gestures. G-FEEDPLACE (app-local), A09-P03. Built in A09-P03 (app-local): Feeding drops three pellets per tap (at most 12), sinks them at 0.5 units/s, lets fish seek the nearest pellet within 4 units and eat it, and removes the rest at the floor; DecorEditing places, moves and removes decor inside the tank with at most 12 pieces; AquariumGestures routes tap → feed, long press → place and a drag on a piece → move through GestureArbiter, and every gesture action has a native control (FeedingTests, DecorEditingTests, AquariumGestureTests, AquariumRenderTests). The arbiter reports a drag's changed phase once, so the aquarium sends a move for every later finger movement itself.

matrix.capability: Bubbles and environmental particles: rising, wobbling bubbles from vents that end at the surface, and slow drifting motes, bounded per quality level
matrix.notes: Emitters with line and ring shapes, buoyancy as negative gravity, drift as wind and the particle budget exist and are tested; the bubble wobble, surface end and mote look are composition in the experience. G-WATERFX (app-local), A09-P04. Built in A09-P04 (app-local): WaterEffects derives bubbles (two vents per habitat, one bubble per vent every 20 steps, rising 1.2 units/s with a ±0.08 wobble, gone at the surface, at most 48) and 24 drifting motes from the step count, so they hold while paused or suspended and never enter the saved state; Reduce Motion halves the rise, removes the wobble and slows the motes (WaterEffectsTests, AquariumRenderTests). Particle counts per quality level arrive with the levels in A09-P05.

matrix.capability: Depth layers: back, middle and front layers with parallax, depth tint and haze, size and speed scaled by depth, drawn in z order
matrix.notes: z order, cameras and the effect passes (blur, colorMatrix, composite) exist and are tested; the layer split, parallax factors and depth tint are the experience's composition. G-WATERFX (app-local), A09-P04. Built in A09-P04 (app-local): fish and plants take depth layer index mod 3, scaled 0.75/0.875/1.0 and tinted 35/15/0 % toward the water colour, drawn back to front with decor and pellets in the middle layer (WaterEffectsTests, AquariumRenderTests). No parallax: the tank has no camera motion.

matrix.capability: Caustics: an animated, seamless light pattern on the sand and fish from procedural noise, with a soft distortion of the water, low-cost on the lowest quality level and still under Reduce Motion
matrix.notes: vc/noise, full-screen shaders and the distort and composite passes exist and are tested; no caustics pattern exists. Built app-local first; it moves to VisualCoreEffects only if a second experience needs it. G-WATERFX (app-local), A09-P04. Built in A09-P04 (app-local): CausticsScene draws the water and gravel with a periodic two-octave noise caustic over a FullScreenShaderScene from inline source, seamless every 16 units, strength 0.04/0.07/0.10 by lighting, time from the step count and fixed under Reduce Motion; a failed shader falls back to the plain clear and gravel (AquariumRenderTests). The simplified lowest-quality variant arrives with the levels in A09-P05.

matrix.capability: Persistence: habitat configurations as versioned documents in a named library in per-experience storage, with migration and safe restore (damaged or newer files kept and counted, never a crash)
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 05; cross-cutting: persistence; manual P03 save system
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCorePersistenceTests and VisualCoreExperienceTests; the habitat schema is G-HABITAT (M09). Storage quota 16 MB, 64 files.

matrix.capability: Low-motion, low-power ambient mode with automatic dimming: reduced frame work and particle counts, slower calmer movement, in-scene brightness dimmed after a period without touch and restored on touch; never the system screen brightness
matrix.source: v0.1 feature 06; manual P05 ambient device testing
matrix.notes: Quality levels, Low Power Mode, Reduce Motion and a brightness cap exist and are tested; no idle timer or dimming policy exists, and the ambient mode's rules are the experience's. G-AMBIENT (app-local), A09-P05.

matrix.capability: Quality tiers and low power: quality governor fed by thermal state and Low Power Mode, declared quality profile, particle budget, session refresh
matrix.source: cross-cutting: quality tiers and low power
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreDiagnosticsTests (QualityGovernorTests) and VisualCoreExperienceHostTests. Core.qualityTiers must match the presenter's levels (declared at P05).

matrix.capability: Accessibility and Reduce Motion: system preferences observed, motion reduced, flashes limited, announcements and haptics through injectable sinks
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreEffectsGraph and VisualCoreUI tests.

matrix.capability: Spoken habitat description: VoiceOver text for the habitat (species and counts, plants and decor, feeding state, ambient mode), rate-limited announcements of changes
matrix.notes: AnnouncementSink and AnnouncementPlanner are public and tested (VisualCoreUITests/AccessibilityPlayersTests, VisualCoreSimulationTests); the habitat wording is experience domain, as Oscilloscope Studio's ScopeAnnouncer is. G-HABITATA11Y (app-local), A09-P04. Built in A09-P04 (app-local): AquariumWording names habitat, species with counts, plants, decorations, food, lighting and motion; AquariumAnnouncer speaks changes (food dropped, habitat, decoration added or removed, paused, swimming) at most once per 3 s through the injected AnnouncementSink, only with VoiceOver on (AquariumWordingTests, AquariumAnnouncerTests, AquariumAnnouncementTests). Ambient mode wording arrives in A09-P05.

matrix.capability: Lifecycle and context loss: context loss, resize, background and memory warning rebuild everything from CPU state; checkpoint on background
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreRendering and VisualCoreExperienceHost tests.

matrix.capability: Licenses and provenance: every species definition, palette, preset habitat and shader bundled later records its author and license (original content only), and third-party notices appear in the app's acknowledgements
matrix.source: cross-cutting: licenses/provenance; manual risk asset licensing; manual P01 content license audit; spec FR-A09-006
matrix.notes: LicenseInventory and AcknowledgementsView cover third-party notices (scripts/check_licenses.py audits the built app); per-content author and license fields for species, palettes, preset habitats and shaders do not exist and belong to the habitat document. G-HABITAT (app-local), A09-P01. Built in A09-P01 (app-local): every species, plant and starter habitat carries author and license (allowed: MIT, VisualCore project); CatalogDecoder refuses missing or unsupported licenses; LicenseAudit generates docs/apps/digital-aquarium/content-licenses.md, which a test keeps equal to the catalog (LicenseAuditTests).

gaps.justification: The habitat document, the two-species catalog and each content item's author and license are Digital Aquarium's domain (manual P01 habitat model and content license audit); shapes, seeds, palettes and persistence come from VisualCore.
gaps.test: Host tests: the habitat document round-trips (format 1) and rejects out-of-range counts, bounds and non-finite values; the same seed builds the same habitat digest; the catalog holds exactly two species with plants; every species, palette and preset habitat records an author and a license and the license audit fails on a missing one

gaps.justification: Found in A09-P00: no neighbour search, steering or flocking exists in any framework product; bounded steering over a neighbour grid is generic (schools, swarms, crowds) and belongs to VisualCoreSimulation.
gaps.test: Host tests: the neighbour grid returns exactly the agents within the radius (checked against brute force) with a per-agent cap; separation, alignment, cohesion, wander and boundary forces have the expected sign and bound; speed and turn rate never exceed their limits; NaN/Inf rejected; seeded runs are deterministic; bounded work per step and no allocation in the steady state (API baseline additive)

gaps.justification: Fish outlines and their body-wave animation are species-specific; they are built from VisualCoreScenes polygons on the VisualCoreSimulation clock.
gaps.test: Host tests: each species outline is a simple polygon within the point cap for every phase of the swim cycle; tail-beat frequency follows speed within limits; turning is smooth (bounded heading change per step); outlines are deterministic per seed

gaps.justification: Feeding and decoration placement are the aquarium's interaction model over the shared gestures, hit testing and view-to-world mapping.
gaps.test: Host tests: a tap drops a bounded number of pellets that sink and are removed when eaten or at the floor; fish seek the nearest pellet within range; decor is placed, moved and removed only inside tank bounds with a bounded count; gesture conflicts resolve through GestureArbiter

gaps.justification: Depth layers, bubbles and caustics are the aquarium's composition over the shared particle system, renderer and effect passes; a caustics pattern moves to VisualCoreEffects only if it proves reusable.
gaps.test: Host tests: bubble and mote counts stay within the particle budget per quality level and bubbles end at the surface; layer order, parallax and depth tint follow depth; simulator tests: the caustics shader compiles and its pattern tiles seamlessly, holds still under Reduce Motion and is skipped or simplified on the lowest quality level

gaps.justification: The habitat wording is experience domain; AnnouncementSink and AnnouncementPlanner already exist in VisualCore.
gaps.test: Host tests of the habitat description for each state (empty decor, feeding, ambient, Reduce Motion) and rate-limited announcements through a RecordingAnnouncementSink

gaps.justification: The ambient mode's motion, particle and dimming rules are the experience's policy over QualityGovernor, DeviceConditions, Reduce Motion and the in-scene brightness cap.
gaps.test: Host tests: ambient mode lowers particle counts and movement speed within stated bounds, Low Power Mode and Reduce Motion select it, the in-scene brightness dims after the idle interval and restores on touch, and the system screen brightness is never changed; frame-cost bounds are recorded for the device campaign

negative.source: constitution A09; CLAUDE.md rule 4; spec FR-A09-006

negative.rule: No ProjectM types, engine or presets and no ProjectM code reused
negative.source: constitution A09 consumer, not fork; CLAUDE.md rule 12; spec FR-A09-006

negative.rule: No networking, accounts, online or multi-user aquarium, analytics, tracking or advertising
negative.source: manual non-goal: online multi-user aquarium; CLAUDE.md rule 3; spec FR-A09-006

negative.rule: No purchased, generated or hand-made artwork: fish, plants, decor, bubbles and caustics are procedural code (shapes, SDFs, noise, particles)
negative.source: CLAUDE.md rule 4; manual risk asset licensing; spec FR-A09-006

negative.rule: License rule: every species definition, palette, preset habitat and shader bundled later records its author and license; only original content is bundled
negative.source: manual P01 content license audit; spec FR-A09-006

negative.rule: No creature economy: no purchasable, collectible, consumable or time-gated creatures, food or decor; the premium unlock is the app's single non-consumable
negative.source: manual non-goal: purchasable creature economy; CLAUDE.md rule 3; spec FR-A09-006

negative.rule: No claims of realistic animal behaviour or an ecosystem simulation, no animal-care guidance, and no health, wellbeing, relaxation or sleep benefit claims; the habitat is an illustrative display
negative.source: manual non-goal: realistic ecosystem or animal-care simulator; spec FR-A09-006 and edge cases

negative.rule: No permission prompts and no system setting changes: no microphone, camera, photos or location, and the ambient mode dims only its own scene, never the system screen brightness
No fork or copy of VisualCore, ANGLE or projectm-ios, no standalone app target and no copy of A04 particle-editor or other experience code; generic needs become VisualCore gaps
negative.source: ADR-0009; constitution A09 reuse first; CLAUDE.md rule 1; spec edge cases

reasons: A working host and drawing path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal, PrimitiveRenderer drawing a SceneNode tree in one batch through Camera2D, ParticleRenderer, full-screen shader scenes and the effect passes, all public and tested.

10 of 20 rows are available with tests: object shapes, the seeded fixed-step clock and easing, procedural environment helpers, particles, scene management, gestures with hit testing, persistence, quality tiers and low power, accessibility and lifecycle.

All gaps are additive and owned: G-STEERING (bounded steering with a neighbour search, VisualCoreSimulation, upstream) in A09-P02; app-local G-HABITAT (habitat document, species catalog, content licenses) in A09-P01, G-FISHSWIM in A09-P02, G-FEEDPLACE in A09-P03, G-WATERFX (depth layers, bubbles, caustics) and G-HABITATA11Y in A09-P04, G-AMBIENT in A09-P05.

No permission and no privacy answer changes; Digital Aquarium stays unregistered until A09-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/DigitalAquarium with its targets and first real domain rules, so the experience package check and the one app are unchanged.
